raw_text:
Here is a complete, ready-to-use 12-week upper-body strength program for your 29-year-old recreational climber client with right subacromial impingement. The plan balances pain-free loading, scapular stability, rotator cuff health, climbing-specific prep, hangboard work, cardio for longer climbing days, mobility, and a Saturday finisher that keeps things engaging. It’s designed for full gym access with consistent weekly structure and clear progression.

Overview and structure
- Phases
  - Phase 1: Foundation & symptom reduction (Weeks 1–4)
  - Phase 2: Load & symmetry with climbing prep (Weeks 5–8)
  - Phase 3: Peak climbing readiness with higher-intensity push work and climber-specific prep (Weeks 9–12)
- Weekly template (Mon–Sun)
  - Session A: Push emphasis (pain-free, non-overhead loading; neutral grip options)
  - Session B: Pull emphasis (horizontal pulling; avoid overhead strain)
  - Session C: Posterior chain / upper-body strength with accessory work
  - Cardio (2x/week): Cardio A and Cardio B (non-consecutive days)
  - Mobility: integrated daily routines; longer mobility block in Phase 3
  - Hangboard & climbing prep: integrated 2x/week in Phase 2–3
  - Saturday Finisher: optional, full-body finisher day (weeks 1–12 rotate)

Detailed week-by-week plan

Phase 1: Foundation & symptom reduction (Weeks 1–4)
Purpose: Restore control, scapular stability, rotator cuff endurance, and establish pain-free loading patterns.

Weeks 1–2
Session A (Push)
- Warm-up: band pull-aparts 2x15; scapular push-ups 2x12; band dislocations 2x10
- Floor press with dumbbells or chest-supported incline: 3x8–10 (light–moderate)
- Serratus anterior activation: push-up plus 3x12
- Tricep extension (cable/rope): 3x12
- Pallof press: 3x10 per side
- External rotator work: sidelying external rotation 2x15
- Core: dead bug 2x12 each side

Session B (Pull)
- Warm-up: band Rows 2x15; reverse fly 2x12
- Seated cable row: 3x10–12
- Dumbbell bent-over row (supported chest): 3x8–10
- Face pulls: 3x12
- Band external rotation at 0–15°: 2x15
- Pallof press: 3x10 per side
- Prone I/T/Y: 2x12

Session C (Posterior chain + accessory)
- Grip/forearm: farmer’s carry 2x30–45s
- Trap/upper back: dumbbell Shrugs 3x12
- Prone rear delt raises 3x12
- Anti-rotation planks: 3x20–30s
- Band-assisted scapula push-ups: 2x12
- Mobility: 5–7 minutes

Weeks 3–4
Progression: small load increase if pain-free; maintain tempo; pause reps on bench/floor press if needed.

Session A (Push)
- Floor press or incline press: 4x6–8
- Neutral-grip incline press (or seated press with scapular support): 3x8
- Serratus plus push-ups: 3x12
- Tricep extension: 3x12
- Pallof press: 3x10 per side
- External rotator work: 2x20

Session B (Pull)
- Machine cable row or barbell row: 4x8–10
- Dumbbell incline row: 3x8–10
- Face pulls: 3x12
- Band pull-aparts: 2x15
- Neutral-grip pulldowns (low/forward): 2x10
- Prone I/T/Y: 2x12

Session C (Posterior chain + core)
- Romanian deadlift to light block or trap-bar from floor: 4x8
- Anti-extension planks: 3x30–45s
- Pallof press: 3x10 per side
- Scapular push-ups: 2x12

Cardio
- Cardio A: 25–30 minutes easy–moderate, RPE 4–5
- Cardio B: 20–25 minutes steady state, choose low-shoulder-load options (bike/elliptical)

Mobility
- Daily warm-up (5–10 minutes): scapular wall slides, band pull-aparts, thoracic thread-the-needle, doorway pec stretch, hip flexor, ankle mobility
- Post-session (5–8 minutes): thoracic foam-rolling, doorway pec stretch, lat stretch
- Phase 1 emphasis on thoracic extension, scapular control, and hip–ankle mobility

Phase 2: Load & symmetry (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Build more resistance with controlled tempo, balance shoulder symmetry, and introduce climbing prep and light hangboard work (no pain).

Weeks 5–6
Session A (Push)
- Floor press or short-range incline press: 4x6–8
- Neutral-grip incline press: 4x8
- Serratus activation: 3x12
- Tricep pushdowns: 3x12
- Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- External rotator work: 2x15–20

Session B (Pull)
- Barbell row or T-bar row: 4x6–8
- Supported single-arm row: 3x8–10 per side
- Face pulls: 3x12
- External rotation: 2x15–20
- Incline/chest-supported pulling: 2x10
- Prone I/T/Y: 2x12

Session C (Posterior chain/upper body)
- Romanian deadlift: 4x6–8
- Farmer’s carry: 2x40–60s
- Core anti-rotation: Pallof 3x12 per side
- Band-assisted push-ups: 2x12
- Mobility/rotator cuff activation: 8 minutes

Weeks 7–8
Session A (Push)
- Floor press: 4x6–8
- Cable/dumbbell incline press: 3x8–10
- Serratus activation: 3x12
- Tricep extensions: 3x12
- Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- External rotator work: 2x20

Session B (Pull)
- Barbell row: 4x6–8
- Single-arm row: 3x8–10 per side
- Face pulls: 3x12
- External rotation: 2x20
Session C (Posterior chain)
- Romanian deadlift or hip hinge variation: 4x6–8
- Shrugs: 3x12
- Anti-rotation planks: 3x40s
- Farmer’s carry: 2x40–60s

Hangboard & climbing prep (Phase 2)
- Hangboard 2x/week
  - Very light to begin: 2–3 mm edges and pockets
  - Protocol: 7 seconds on, 3 seconds off; 6–8 reps per set; 3 sets; 2–3 minutes rest
  - Gradually progress to 6–7 seconds on, 3–4 off; 4–5 sets
- Climbing prep: light technique work, lock-offs, scapular control, body-position drills

Mobility (Phase 2)
- 10–15 minutes, 2–3x/week; thoracic flossing, sleeper stretch (gentle), doorway chest, scapular wall slides with end-range hold, lat stretch, hip mobility

Phase 3: Peak readiness, climber focus, and taper (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Peak climbing performance with higher-intensity push work early in the phase, then taper for Week 12 climbing trip.

Weeks 9–10
Session A (Push – peak-intensity introduction)
- Floor press or incline press (neutral grip): 4x4–6 (RPE 8/10; pain-free)
- Dumbbell bench press neutral grip: 3x6–8
- Serratus push-ups: 3x12
- Tricep pushdowns: 3x10
- Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- External rotator work: 2x15

Session B (Pull)
- Barbell row: 4x6–8
- Seated cable row: 3x8–10
- Face pulls: 3x12
- External rotation: 2x20

Session C (Upper-body strength & conditioning)
- Romanian deadlift: 4x6–8
- Farmer’s carry: 2x60s
- Core anti-rotation: Pallof 3x12 per side
- Band-assisted push-ups: 2x12

Hangboard: 2x/week; keep grip variety and load within tolerance

Week 11
- Push: volume tapers; maintain strength
  - Floor press: 3x5–6
  - Neutral-grip incline press: 3x6–8
  - Serratus push-ups: 3x12
  - Tricep pushdowns: 3x10
  - Pallof press: 3x12 per side
- Pull: Barbell row: 3x6–8; Seated row: 3x8–10; Face pulls: 3x12
- Climber-focused conditioning: technique blocks, light endurance climbs; scapular stability emphasis
- Hangboard: 2x/week with a deload set in one of the sets

Week 12 (Peak week for climbing trip)
- Push (low volume, high control)
  - Floor press: 2x4–6
  - Neutral-grip incline: 2x6
  - Serratus push-ups: 2x12
  - Tricep extensions: 2x10
  - Pallof press: 2x12 per side
- Pull
  - Barbell row: 3x5
  - Seated row: 2x8
  - Face pulls: 2x12
  - External rotation: 2x20
- Climbing-specific taper
  - Short technique-focused climbs, light volume, movement quality
- Hangboard: reduce duration/intensity to taper
- Mobility: continue as usual; ensure shoulder feels fresh

Cardio integration (2x/week)
- Cardio A: 25–40 minutes, mostly LISS
- Cardio B: 20–30 minutes steady-state; can include light climbing-specific tempo on a bike ergometer or similar
- Schedule: align with non-heavy upper-body days; avoid heavy loading after high-intensity push sessions

Saturday Finisher (full-body, optional; Weeks 1–12)
- After main session or stand-alone on Saturdays, 20–40 minutes depending on phase
- Structure: 6–8 stations, 30–60 seconds each, 1–3 rounds
- Example stations (phase-appropriate): bodyweight squats, farmer’s carry, pallof press hold, slam ball, planks, band dislocations, wall climbs or footwork drills, mobility finisher
- Intensity: RPE 5–7/10; focus on movement quality and fun while maintaining shoulder health

Mobility plan (as integrated)
- Phase-aligned daily mobility: front-loaded in warm-ups; phase 3 includes daily 8–12 minutes plus a longer weekly 15–20 minute mobility block
- Thoracic mobility, scapular control, rotator cuff health, hip/ankle mobility, and posture work emphasized
- Pain-free ranges only; adjust intensity and ranges if symptoms appear

Nutrition and recovery (for recomposition, ongoing)
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, distributed across meals every 3–4 hours
- Calorie target: near maintenance or modest deficit (0–300 kcal/day), adjusted weekly based on rate of weight change and climbing performance
- Carbs: aligned with training load; higher on climbing days
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; aim for unsaturated fats
- Hydration: 35–45 ml/kg/day plus electrolytes around training
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; recovery-focused routines on rest days
- 1–2 refeed or maintenance days if clustering fatigue or performance dips

Progression and load management
- Pain-free progressions: aim for gradual weekly increases in load when form remains perfect and symptoms stay absent
- If symptoms flare: back off to last pain-free acceptable load and volume, and emphasize mobility and scapular stability
- Regular check-ins: monitor ROM, pain, performance, climbing endurance, and overall fatigue; adjust volumes as needed

Equipment considerations
- Gym: dumbbells, barbells, cable machines, floor press options, bands, hangboard, kettlebell, medicine ball, TRX/ bands for rows and mobility
- If hangboard or climbing-specific equipment is limited, substitution options include campus-style isometrics on safe grips or resistance-band finger strength work

Deliverables and further customization
- I can convert Weeks 9–12 into a precise day-by-day schedule with exact sets/reps/rest, plus a printable one-page summary you can hand to the climber.
- I can tailor grip selections, hangboard protocol, and weekend finisher specifics to the climber’s exact equipment (edge depths, pocket types, slopers), as well as her current 1RM estimates.

Would you like me to produce a fully detailed, print-ready Week 1–12 summary with exact daily workouts, rest intervals, and a 1-page climber-focused summary for your client? If you share her current 1RM estimates or recent 1–2 rep maxes for bench or floor press, I’ll tailor the plan precisely to her metrics.
